sermon.title: What God’s Word Does to the Gentiles
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues through Isaiah to show how God deals with the Gentiles, including religionists who change His word like Esau, and says the church’s part is to speak the gospel to them. Using Isaiah 35 he says God’s “vengeance” is the desert blossoming like a rose, the highway of holiness and everlasting joy for the redeemed.

faqs.question: Why does he say Christ cannot come any minute?
faqs.answer: He says Isaiah’s prophecies “has not been accomplished globally,” and that the idea that the rapture can happen any minute “is just full of baloney” because “there’s a lot of stuff that’s got to be done yet.” He adds that God can do it quickly but still has to do it.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And all nations shall flow to it. Many people shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. He shall judge between the nations, And rebuke many people; They shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruning hooks; Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war anymore.

faqs.question: What does he say our birthright is?
faqs.answer: He says it is that “if we believe on the Lord Jesus Christ that God has raised him from the dead, we shall be saved,” and also “keeping the commandments.” He says bringing forth fruit suitable for repentance is “just as important as believing,” and neglecting it is neglecting our birthright.

scriptures.text_nkjv: that if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.

faqs.question: Why does he expect a large harvest in the last days?
faqs.answer: He says there are over 7 billion people now, and “billions of people in these last 100 years” beyond all who lived before, so when God says Gentiles in heaven “cannot be numbered,” he is going to manifest Himself in these last days. He says looking for Jesus to come in a minute misses the purpose of God to fill heaven with people.

faqs.question: What does he say about reading the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says it is “the most precious book in the world,” yet we make time for baseball, football and soap operas and “no time to read God’s word.” He says we read other authors but can open the Bible and find out what it says.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Search from the book of the LORD, and read: Not one of these shall fail; Not one shall lack her mate. For My mouth has commanded it, and His Spirit has gathered them.

faqs.question: How does he say people twist scripture?
faqs.answer: He says putting in your own opinions is “adding to the word,” and taking verses out of the Bible is “taken away from the word.” He says if people follow us after we alter it, “we’re leading them to destruction.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things, in which are some things hard to understand, which untaught and unstable people twist to their own destruction, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures.

faqs.question: What does he say about the saying that all roads lead to the same God?
faqs.answer: He says “they change the scriptures” and that “all roads lead to the same God” is a statement a lot of leaders make “not understanding it comes directly from” another religion, not the Bible. His view is stated as he spoke it and is not verified here.

faqs.question: How does he explain the Trinity?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus is God, God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Ghost, and asks “how many gods?” and answers “one.” He says “we’re not talking about three gods,” though we may use the word Trinity.

faqs.question: Does he say Paul wrote some things as his own opinion?
faqs.answer: He says in 1 Corinthians Paul wrote “I write this, not the Lord,” giving his own permission, but that the rest God was telling him to write, so the writers wrote “as the Holy Spirit gave him the inspiration.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But to the rest I, not the Lord, say: If any brother has a wife who does not believe, and she is willing to live with him, let him not divorce her.

faqs.question: How does he define love?
faqs.answer: He says love is not “that fear feeling” but “that principle of doing nothing and speaking nothing to hurt others.” He says you don’t have to have vibes or feelings, “you just do it.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For the commandments, “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not bear false witness,” “You shall not covet,” and if there is any other commandment, are all summed up in this saying, namely, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.

faqs.question: Does he say our sin hurts God?
faqs.answer: He says God is not “up on the throne worried” and that “your bad choices hurt you and they hurt others.” He says God’s plan cannot be rattled: “he knows what he’s doing, he knows where he’s going.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? Or, if your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to Him? If you are righteous, what do you give Him? Or what does He receive from your hand? Your wickedness affects a man such as you, And your righteousness a son of man.

faqs.question: Why does he say chapter breaks do not change the subject?
faqs.answer: He says “a chapter does not separate necessarily a subject. Chapters are put in there by man,” so Isaiah 35 continues the subject of God’s visitation on the Gentiles from Isaiah 34.

faqs.question: What does he say the desert is a picture of in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says the desert “is always referred to as a place where you get tested and humbled during life’s difficulties.” He says God led Israel 40 years in the wilderness to “know what was in their heart, not to seduce them with sin.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let no one say when he is tempted, “I am tempted by God”; for God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He Himself tempt anyone.

faqs.question: Does he say every bad thing that happens is because of sin?
faqs.answer: He says no: “it’s not our own choice, it’s not God, and it’s not sin” in every case. He cites the tower that fell, saying “it wasn’t their sin that the tower fell,” and that an accident can “just happen.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them, do you think that they were worse sinners than all other men who dwelt in Jerusalem? I tell you, no; but unless you repent you will all likewise perish.”

faqs.question: Does he say we should look down on people of other beliefs?
faqs.answer: He says no: “we got no right looking down on the Mormons,” or anybody. He says if we have truth, “the key to their survival is us speaking it, sharing it.”

faqs.question: What does he say about people moving from church to church?
faqs.answer: He says in America “Christianity is not growing, all we’re doing is moving from one church to another,” and cites a drop from 86% to 78% saying “we are not saving souls in America.” These are his figures as spoken, without a source.
